analysis.title: GS Coppersmith - US EQUITIES panic / positioning 22 Nov 2026
key_insights: SPX is below 7k and the GS Vol Panic Index finished Friday at 9.8 out of 10. Panic of this magnitude has historically been a good opportunity to start adding risk.
The Fed is hiking rather than cutting. In five episodes where panic exceeded 9 during a hiking regime, subsequent three-month returns averaged just +0.4%.
Hedge funds have been through an enormous unwind. Short sales outpaced long buying 1.5 to 1, US single stocks were shorted every day last week, and ETF shorts rose 11% on the week.
Fundamental L/S net leverage fell to 42.3% (1st percentile over past year). Beta-adjusted net leverage fell more than 22 pts since early October to 48.2%, a five-year low.
Momentum exposure reversed from a record +70% in June to negative, the lowest since late 2022. The HF VIP basket underperformed SPX by 14pp over six months.
Fundamental L/S lost 1.2% on Friday and is down 2.1% MTD. US-focused managers lost 1.6%, a 2.6 standard deviation move. Systematic L/S is up 1.5% MTD.

Other cohorts remain well invested. The GS US Equity Sentiment Indicator is at the 75th percentile, mutual funds and ETFs took in nearly $170bn since the start of Q4, and asset manager futures length is at the 82nd percentile.

The setup shows HF capitulation but not the broad investor washout that has historically produced the strongest rebounds. Q4 2018 is a cited parallel: the October 2018 panic was followed by another 6.8% decline over three months.

High-Beta Cyclicals are up 12% YTD while broad US AI is negative YTD. In 4Q-2018 high beta cyclicals fell 23%. At 15x fwd PE the basket is a 40% premium to its 2018 trough multiple, so it is vulnerable if growth fears replace inflation fears.
GS Research frames SPX at roughly 5,800 if valuations normalize to the 30-year average, versus 8,100 if confidence in consensus earnings and multiples recovers.

CTAs are short US equities and would be buyers on a bounce, with the remaining supply risk mostly outside the US. Dealer gamma is negative into a holiday-shortened week and S&P futures top-of-book depth is at its lowest since April 2025.

Vol looks overshot. VXN finished at the highest since COVID, VXSMH hit an all-time high, and the front of the vol curve is sharply inverted. GS prefers underwriting vol via put sales over buying delta, and sees a near tactical entry.

sector_views.rationale: Up 12% YTD at 15x fwd PE, a 40% premium to the 2018 trough. Would underperform sharply if growth uncertainty displaces inflation anxiety, as in 4Q-2018.
Vol repricing is most extreme here, which makes put selling at comfortable entry levels attractive, though AI earnings uncertainty remains.

earnings_insights: AI earnings debate centers on 2027/28 AI earnings, capex and monetization. GS Research sees SPX near 5,800 on normalized valuation versus 8,100 on recovered consensus confidence (scenario estimates, not reported results).

macro_indicators.interpretation: A hiking Fed weakens the usual panic-to-rebound pattern, with average 3-month returns of +0.4% in comparable episodes.
Wide distribution of outcomes tied to AI earnings confidence and valuation multiples.

trade_ideas.description: Sell downside puts in tech and semis at levels where the desk would add length, underwriting elevated implied vol rather than buying delta
trade_ideas.rationale: Implied vol is panicked, so the hurdle for owning protection is high and put sellers are paid more to take equity risk with lower entry levels.
trade_ideas.risk: A more sustained selloff would leave the seller with downside risk.

risk_factors: Fed is hiking and has not come to the rescue.
Broader investor positioning remains elevated, so there is no broad washout.
Unresolved AI earnings, capex and monetization debate.
Negative dealer gamma and thin S&P futures liquidity in a holiday week.
Q4 2018 parallel of another leg lower after panic.
Possible CTA supply outside the US.
vol_and_positioning: GS Vol Panic Index finished Friday at 9.8 out of 10.
VXN finished Friday at the highest level since COVID. VXSMH finished at its series all-time high.
Front of the vol curve is sharply inverted, so the market is paying a large premium for near-term protection.
Dealer gamma is negative entering a shortened holiday week. S&P futures top-of-book depth is at the lowest since April 2025.
HF fundamental L/S net leverage 42.3%, 1st percentile over one year. Beta-adjusted net leverage 48.2%, a five-year low.
Single stock shorting was the largest weekly since June 2022. ETF shorts rose 11% on the week.
CTAs are short US equities and would be buyers on a bounce. Remaining supply risk sits outside the US.
Idea: sell puts at levels where adding length is comfortable, especially in tech where vol repricing is most extreme.

tension_points.bull_case: Vol panic at 9.8 out of 10 and HF net leverage at multi-year lows. CTAs are short US equities and would buy a bounce, and panic has historically been a good time to add risk.
tension_points.bear_case: Fed is hiking, and other cohorts remain well invested (sentiment at 75th percentile, $170bn inflows). Q4 2018 saw another 6.8% decline after panic, and AI earnings are unresolved.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A broader sustained selloff with continued positioning reduction and no dovish Fed or AI earnings reassurance, which would hurt short put positions.
